title: 100,000+ Movie Reviews from Kazakhstan: Russian, Kazakh, and Code-Switched Texts

model.params_source: assumed (the paper states no decoding parameters); max_tokens 4 because the prompt allows exactly one digit

task.subset_rule: all: the full released corpus (Table 1 total = 100,502 reviews; ru 96,749 / kk 2,639 / code-switched 1,114)
task.approximation: at 3 seeds this is 301,506 calls; the runner's per-paper cap will cut a seeded random subset unless the cap is raised for this paper

items.config_or_split: config full, split train (100,502 rows, 26.0 MB parquet)
items.gated: auto - huggingface.co/api/datasets/... reports gated='auto'; anonymous file reads return HTTP 401 and a token for this project's account returns HTTP 403, i.e. the dataset terms have not been accepted for that account
items.fields_source: the columns are read from the dataset card's dataset_info (review_text, review_date, review_user_id, review_language, review_user_score, review_sentiment, movie_id, movie_title_ru, movie_title_en, movie_theatrical_release_year, movie_genre, movie_director, movie_duration_min, movie_age_rating, movie_production_country, annotation_note)

prompt.system: You are a sentiment classifier for movie reviews (Russian or Kazakh). Return one digit only: 2 - clearly positive / recommends the movie; 1 - neutral, mixed, or unclear; 0 - clearly negative / does not recommend. Always choose one digit; never output anything else.
prompt.source_location: Sec. 3, inline ('The model was instructed as follows: ...')
prompt.verbatim: full for the system prompt (printed inline in Sec. 3; the printed en-dashes after each digit are kept as hyphens). The user message is assumed to be the review text alone - the paper does not print it.

placeholders_paper.review: the review text of the row

output.postprocess: strip; a reply that is not one of the three digits counts as incorrect
output.parse_paper: the model is instructed to emit a single digit

metric.name: accuracy
metric.definition: share of the 100,502 reviews whose predicted digit equals the single annotator's sentiment label (negative=0, neutral=1, positive=2)
metric.original_location: Sec. 3, inline ('GPT-generated labels achieved 89.54% accuracy relative to the single-annotator labels over the full corpus, with substantial agreement (Cohen's kappa = 0.78)')

open_points: gated dataset: yeshpanovrustem/100k_movie_reviews_from_kz is gated with auto-approval, so a human has to open the dataset page with the project's Hugging Face account and accept the terms once. Until then every file read is 401/403 and --prepare cannot fetch the rows.

label vocabulary: the three review_sentiment values are taken to be 'negative' / 'neutral' / 'positive' from the column headers of Table 1; the actual strings in the parquet could not be read because of the gate, so items.label_map must be checked on the first successful download.

cost cap: the full corpus at 3 seeds is 301,506 calls (about USD 7 at gpt-4.1-nano prices but far above the usual per-paper cap); decide whether to run the full corpus, a single seed, or a seeded subsample with the CI carried through.
notes: gpt-4.1-nano is used in the paper as a second annotation pass rather than for a headline result, but the 89.54% / kappa 0.78 comparison against the single-annotator labels is a complete, fully specified classification claim over a released corpus. Cohen's kappa is a second reproducible quantity from the same outputs (not one of the runner's metrics; it would need a hook).
